findings.title: Bare `np.ndarray` return annotations will fail strict pyright
findings.description: `_array` and `_mask` are annotated `-> np.ndarray` with no type arguments. `pyproject.toml` sets `typeCheckingMode = "strict"` and includes `tests`, and the Python rules make zero pyright errors a merge blocker. Strict mode reports `reportMissingTypeArgument` for the bare generic. The sibling helpers in `tests/core_model/test_labels.py` already use `NDArray[np.float64]` and `NDArray[np.bool_]`. Use those types here too.

findings.title: Test exercises Python's `match` statement, not project code
findings.description: The test builds a local `match output:` with its own branches and asserts on the strings it built. It calls no production code, so it passes whatever `declarations.py` does. If the intent is to prove the three output forms support structural matching, it only shows that dataclasses with `slots=True` have `__match_args__`. That is language behavior. Either remove it, or move the `match` into a real consumer (for example a describe helper in the catalog slice) and test that.

findings.title: Output validation depends on `OutputDeclaration.__value__`
findings.description: `isinstance(item, OutputDeclaration.__value__)` works today because the alias is a `|` union. It relies on the `type`-statement alias internals, and pyright strict may not model it well. A module-level constant would be clearer: `_OUTPUT_TYPES: Final = (SeriesOutput, LabelOutput, SignalOutput)`. The alias could then be written in terms of it. That would also keep the list of output forms in one place, as the "define once" rule asks.

findings.title: `assert` used for type narrowing in production code
findings.description: `assert isinstance(series, Series)` follows a `require_instance` call that has already raised for any non-`Series`. It exists only to narrow the type. It is stripped under `python -O` and is harmless at runtime. A `cast`, or having `require_instance` return a narrowed value, would avoid assert-as-control-flow.

findings.title: Several classes per module versus the one-class-per-file rule
findings.description: The module holds seven small, closely related frozen dataclasses and enums, and stays under 300 lines. This is a reasonable grouping and matches the "group related tiny utilities" exception. It is recorded only because the Python rules say one class per file for models.

findings.title: Shared validation, vectorized checks and boundary tests
findings.description: `check_confidence` is written once and reused by both label series and signal sequences. `as_integer` and `as_real` are the single coercion path, and `bind_parameters` collects every issue instead of failing on the first. The AST-based tests that forbid element loops and `CANONICAL_TYPE` give mechanical enforcement of design decisions D4 and D10. The import-boundary test list was extended to cover the new modules.
